label: Explicit business-integrated digital strategy
text_anchor: "a governing role over initiatives", "a multi-year horizon" and "is openly communicated". The narrative adds detailed goal communication (N4), strategy review (N5) and external technology positioning (N6).
use_or1: The strategy owners decide in the portfolio review on every initiative without a goal link and on every goal link beyond its horizon, and the decision produces a clarification task for the named initiative owner.
information_or2: Goal, strategic assumption, time horizon, next review date, addressed roles and review decision, bound to goal, initiative and role.
producer_or3: The strategy owner creates and answers for the goal record including its horizon, the initiative owner confirms the goal link of their initiative, and the review body creates the review decision in its minutes.

label: Continuously sustained business-IT alignment
text_anchor: "sustained as a continuous, multidimensional process" and "active misalignment sensing and correction". N4 treats misalignment as a normal recurring incident with an explicit sensing step and periodic reappraisal of applications against the functions they serve.
use_or1: The responsible architect reappraises at a set cadence whether the recorded links still hold across all four alignment domains — business strategy to IT strategy, and organisational to IS infrastructure — and decides per finding on correction, change or acceptance, producing a recorded decision with an owner and a due date.
information_or2: Alignment link with the two domains it connects, the review cadence and last review date, the misalignment finding and the decision taken on it, bound to goal, capability, process and application so that all four domains carry links rather than the application layer alone.
producer_or3: The owner of each domain object confirms the links leaving it — the strategy owner for goals, the capability owner for capabilities, the process owner for processes and the application owner for applications — and the reviewing architect creates the misalignment finding.

label: Deliberate operating-model decision
text_anchor: "A deliberate operating-model decision (diversification/coordination/replication/unification)". N2 specifies standardisation and integration.
use_or1: The planning owner decides for every new undertaking whether it follows the established degree of standardisation and integration, and the decision produces a reasoned approval or a recorded deviation with a condition attached.
information_or2: Chosen operating model and degree of standardisation and integration per organisational unit, together with the reasoned deviation decision, bound to organisational unit and undertaking.
producer_or3: The leadership of the organisational unit concerned takes and answers for the operating-model decision; the planning owner creates the deviation decision in the existing approval process.

label: Business model bridging strategy to execution design
text_anchor: "a business model that bridges strategy formulation to execution design". N4 names value proposition, customers, suppliers and activities.
use_or1: The planning owner derives the required capabilities and processes from the business-model elements, and that produces the capability demand an undertaking is scoped against.
information_or2: Business-model elements such as value proposition, customer segment, supplier and core activity, and their link to required capability, process and application.
producer_or3: The business owner for the market offering concerned creates and answers for the business-model description; the planning owner confirms the mapping to capabilities.

label: Explicit value-creation and value-capture logic per initiative
text_anchor: "Explicit value-creation/value-capture logic (appropriability, complementary assets)" and "business-model transformation as a precondition for monetizing digital innovation". N1 asks how an initiative will be monetised, not only how it creates value.
use_or1: The portfolio review decides on continuation for every initiative whose capture logic is unstated or rests on assets the enterprise does not control, and on every initiative that requires a change to the business model without one being recorded, producing a continuation, rework or discontinuation decision with a rationale.
information_or2: Value proposition of the initiative, the named capture mechanism, the complementary assets it depends on and whether the enterprise controls them, and the business-model element the initiative changes with the required change and its status, bound to initiative, a sponsor-confirmed business-model element and the applications that support it.
producer_or3: The Business Stakeholder recorded as the initiative's business sponsor creates and answers for the value statement, confirms the capture mechanism, complementary assets, affected business-model element and supporting applications, and the portfolio lead records the review decision. The existing human-confirmed value statements on initiatives carry the same producer pattern.

label: Non-compensatory allocation of strategic attention
text_anchor: "Deliberate, non-compensatory allocation of strategic attention across transformation domains". N4 notes that priority tends to fall on what the organisation itself controls.
use_or1: Met. The executive leadership would decide where to concentrate attention if its current allocation were established, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. The claim is that strategic attention is allocated deliberately and non-compensatorily across transformation domains. A ranked priority list records what leadership declares, and the initiative and resource distribution records where work goes; neither carries the allocation of attention the claim asserts, and no reasoned operational definition with a reference group and a rule of interpretation is available. Treating the declared ranking as the attention allocation would be an unjustified proxy. CF#311 offers a weighting derived from an expert panel rather than from the enterprise whose attention is at stake.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Explicit design of decision rights
text_anchor: "which decisions exist", "who holds them" and "matched to decision type and performance goal". N4 requires alignment with existing organisational arrangements.
use_or1: Whoever prepares a decision puts it to the responsible right holder and involves the designated input roles, and an expired or unfilled mandate produces a clarification task for the organisational unit that answers for it.
information_or2: Decision domain, right holder, input roles, performance goal pursued and validity period of the mandate, bound to organisational unit, body and person.
producer_or3: The organisational unit that grants the mandate creates and answers for the mandate record within the existing organisational arrangement, and the named right holder confirms their responsibility.

label: Coordinated deployment of structures, processes and relational mechanisms
text_anchor: "Structures, processes, and relational mechanisms deployed as a coordinated set with sufficient practice maturity" and "relational mechanisms ... are necessary, not optional". N3 states that a steering committee cannot decide well without mature supporting processes, N4 that a smaller set recurs as the effective core across all three kinds.
use_or1: The governance owner reviews which of the agreed mechanisms are in place across all three types, which body or forum carries each and which supporting process each decision structure depends on, and decides on the missing ones, producing an implementation task with an owner and a date. For a relational mechanism the same review decides which units it has not yet reached, producing a scheduling task.
information_or2: Governance mechanism with its type — structure, process or relational — the body, process or forum that carries it, its status and cadence, the decision structure it supports, and for a relational mechanism the units and roles it addressed together with the dates it ran, bound to organisational unit, body and role.
producer_or3: The governance function creates and answers for the mechanism inventory; the owner of each body, process or forum confirms that the mechanism is in place; the convening role records each occurrence of a relational mechanism and the units it reached. Recording an occurrence carries that the mechanism ran and whom it addressed, not what it achieved.

label: Principled commitment to the governance principles
text_anchor: "principled commitment are necessary, not optional" in the description. N5 records that mechanisms can be followed to the letter while remaining symbolic.
use_or1: The governance owner administers the commitment instrument against the principle set actually in force and decides per principle which cohort needs renewed grounding, producing a measure with an owner and a date.
information_or2: Instrument with its version and the principle set it is bound to, the suitability rationale for the principles in force here, the items, the responses, the survey date and the result per principle, bound to survey run, respondent cohort, organisational unit and the governance arrangement.
producer_or3: The producers of the information are the members of the responding cohort, who answer the instrument’s items, together with the governance function that administers the survey and answers for its conduct. The instrument itself is not a producer: it is the operational definition that makes the answers interpretable, and CF#184 supplies it as a construct stated against a named five-principle set. Because the instrument is bound to the principle set it was built for, its use here requires a documented rationale that the principles in force are the ones it measures; without that rationale the record holds the gap rather than a commitment result.

label: Transparent governance arrangement
text_anchor: "Transparency of governance mechanisms". N6 warns that judging implementation by framework conformance alone misses this.
use_or1: A manager preparing a decision looks up which body decides it, under which mandate and with which input roles, and where the arrangement names no body the governance function receives a clarification task.
information_or2: Published governance arrangement with decision domain, deciding body, input roles, validity and the version published, bound to organisational unit and body.
producer_or3: The governance function creates and answers for the published arrangement, and each named body confirms its own entry.

label: Accurate managerial understanding of the governance arrangement
text_anchor: "manager/stakeholder understanding and awareness of them as a leading predictor" and the enabling statement's "share of senior managers who can accurately describe it".
use_or1: The governance function compares a manager’s description of who decides a given matter against the published arrangement held under CC09-A1, and decides per deviation on targeted education or on a clarification of the arrangement itself, producing a measure with an owner and a date.
information_or2: Comparison record with the decision domain asked about, the description given, the published entry it was compared against, the deviation found and the measure decided, bound to person, decision domain and the published arrangement.
producer_or3: The responding manager produces the description and remains its source, and the published arrangement supplies the yardstick it is compared against. The governance function answers for the comparison and the measure. The yardstick is an enterprise record rather than an external instrument, which is what makes the accuracy of a description assessable.

label: Actively designed governance with a controlled redesign cadence
text_anchor: "actively designed, simple, educated-about, and redesigned infrequently". N4 admits bounded incremental adjustment when strategy or technology materially changes.
use_or1: The governance owner records each change to the arrangement with its trigger and decides at the annual review whether the accumulated changes are incremental adjustments or amount to a redesign, producing a documented decision either way. The same review decides which roles have not yet been taken through the arrangement, producing an education task with an owner and a date.
information_or2: Change to the governance arrangement with its date, trigger and scope, the review date, the design objectives the arrangement declares, and the education provision with the roles it addressed and the dates it ran, bound to the published arrangement and the addressed role.
producer_or3: The governance function creates and answers for the change record and the declared objectives; the body affected by a change confirms it.

label: Deliberate federated balance of central standards and domain autonomy
text_anchor: "Deliberate balance of centralized standards with decentralized domain autonomy". N3 names the recurring design error of conflating input rights with decision rights.
use_or1: The governance owner records per decision domain who provides input and who decides, and the architecture board decides on every domain where the recorded input right is being exercised as a decision right, producing a correction of the arrangement.
information_or2: Decision domain, the body holding the decision right, the units holding input rights, the standards reserved centrally and the scope left to the domain, bound to organisational unit and decision domain.
producer_or3: The organisational unit granting the mandate creates and answers for the split; each domain confirms the scope it holds.

label: Governance design fitted to recorded contingency factors
text_anchor: "Governance designs contingent on size, maturity, risk appetite, sector, and optimized performance dimension" and "revisited when those conditions change".
use_or1: The governance owner records the contingency factors the current design rests on and the performance goal it optimises, and decides at review whether a changed factor requires the design to be revisited, producing a confirmation or a revision decision.
information_or2: Contingency factor with its recorded value, the performance goal the design optimises, the design choices that rest on each factor and the review date, bound to organisational unit and published arrangement.
producer_or3: The governance function creates and answers for the factor record and the rationale linking factor to design choice; the unit leadership confirms the factor values for its own area.

label: Board and executive engagement under distinct mandates
text_anchor: "Board-level and executive-level engagement with distinct mandates". N3 keeps board-level oversight and executive translation into priorities apart.
use_or1: The governance owner records which body holds oversight and which holds the translation into priorities and resourcing, and raises for decision every matter that reached neither, producing an assignment to the responsible body.
information_or2: Body with its level, the mandate it holds, the matters it decided in the period and the members who carry it, bound to body, organisational unit and decision domain.
producer_or3: The secretary of each body creates and answers for its mandate and its decision record; the unit that constitutes the body confirms the mandate.

label: Single-point accountability and ownership
text_anchor: "Clear single-point accountability and ownership". N5 adds accountability for specified outputs.
use_or1: The responsible area lead reviews which areas of accountability are unfilled or filled more than once, and the review produces an assignment decision with a due date.
information_or2: Area of accountability, accountable person or role, validity period and agreed outputs, bound to the owned object and the person.
producer_or3: The assigning manager creates and confirms the accountability assignment; the accountable person confirms acceptance.

label: Incentives aligned to transformation and standardization goals
text_anchor: "incentives (including soft/recognition-based) aligned to transformation and standardization goals".
use_or1: The responsible role reviews in the goal-setting cycle which declared incentive rule contradicts a transformation or standardisation goal, and the review produces an adjusted goal agreement.
information_or2: Incentive rule as worded, incentive type including non-monetary recognition, addressed role and the link to the named transformation or standardisation goal.
producer_or3: The human-resources function or the programme leadership creates the incentive and recognition rule in the existing goal-setting process and thereby carries the declared rule.

label: Governed decentralized and business-led IT
text_anchor: "information symmetry, ... risk-tiered proportionate control, and enacted decision-right realignment". N2 makes registration of decentrally built applications the first step, N3 the proportionate tiering, N4 the split of responsibilities.
use_or1: The responsible architect assigns a registered, business-built application to a risk tier and decides on the control level that tier requires, producing an approval, a condition or a migration decision with an owner. The same decision records the justification for the control applied and the exception path open to the building unit, and an exception request is decided rather than left unanswered.
information_or2: Registered business-built application with the unit that built it, its risk tier, the controls the tier requires together with the recorded justification for each, the exception path and any exception decided, and the split of responsibilities between the unit and the IT function, bound to application, organisational unit and role.
producer_or3: The building unit registers the application and confirms its purpose; the architect assigns the risk tier and records the justification for the control applied; the IT function and the unit jointly confirm the responsibility split; the exception decision is recorded by whoever holds the right to grant it. What the record carries is the justified, proportionate control with an open exception path — the practice CF#484 describes as transparent, proportionate and co-designed, which governs rather than prohibits.

label: Legitimacy of the arrangement among the units it binds
text_anchor: "legitimacy" in the description and "governed through legitimacy ... rather than prohibition" in the enabling statement. N5: the guardrails are "experienced as enabling rather than obstructive once they are legitimate".
use_or1: Met. The architecture function would decide which controls need renewed grounding or redesign if the standing of the arrangement among the bound units were established, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. The claim concerns how the arrangement stands with the units it binds. Recorded justifications, exception paths and decided exceptions are the practice that may produce that standing. CF#484 states both sides and keeps them apart: guardrails are designed transparent, proportionate and co-designed, and explained governance is then experienced as legitimate and followed voluntarily. N5 separates them likewise: the guardrails are experienced as enabling once they are legitimate, not by being justified. No reasoned operational definition with a reference group, ordered levels and a rule of interpretation is available — the evidence supplies none, and the author has confirmed that the enterprise holds none either, which is the difference from CC48, where an ordered scale and an agreed assessment exist. Inferring legitimacy from a low exception rate or from adherence would be an unjustified proxy, since both are equally consistent with acquiescence.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Senior-body prioritization with architecture-guided oversight
text_anchor: "Elevating strategic IT-project prioritization to the senior governing body" and "architecture-guided investment oversight". N3 makes a shared, accessible guidance library the architecture input.
use_or1: The senior governing body decides the prioritisation of candidate projects against the declared enterprise priorities and the architecture guidance, producing a ranked and recorded portfolio decision with the criteria applied.
information_or2: Candidate project with its sponsoring unit, the enterprise priority it serves, the architecture guidance applied, the prioritisation criteria and the decision taken, bound to initiative, programme and priority.
producer_or3: The portfolio office creates and answers for the candidate list and the applied criteria; the architecture function creates the guidance; the senior body records the decision.

label: Actively managed IT-standards lifecycle
text_anchor: "A dedicated steering structure, lifecycle model, incentive linkage, and proactive communication". N3 runs the lifecycle from initiation and approval through monitored use to retirement.
use_or1: The standards owner moves a standard through its lifecycle stages and decides at each gate on approval, continuation or retirement, producing a recorded stage decision, a communication to the units it binds on introduction, and the incentive rule that links adherence to the standard to the goals of the roles it binds.
information_or2: Standard with its lifecycle stage, owner, approval and retirement dates, the units it binds, the communication issued at introduction, and the incentive rule linking adherence to the goals of the bound roles, bound to standard, organisational unit and role.
producer_or3: The standards office creates and answers for the standard, its stage decisions and the communication; the approving body confirms the approval; the personnel function or the binding unit creates the incentive rule in the existing goal-setting process, as for the incentive rules held under CC14-A2.

label: EA artifacts designed for their audience and purpose
text_anchor: "designed for cognitive fit and usability, acting as boundary objects". N6 requires that what a viewpoint deliberately leaves out is documented as a design decision.
use_or1: The architect registers each artifact with its purpose, audience and the decision it supports, and the review decides on artifacts that no named audience uses, producing a revision or retirement decision.
information_or2: Artifact with its type, purpose, intended audience, the decision it supports and the content its viewpoint deliberately omits, bound to artifact, decision and role.
producer_or3: The authoring architect creates and answers for the artifact record and its stated omissions; the named audience confirms the artifact serves the decision it claims to support.

label: Participative EA development with a maintained shared vocabulary
text_anchor: "Active stakeholder participation, communication richness, and a shared business-IT language in EA development".
use_or1: The architect records which affected stakeholders took part in developing an artifact, which terms the shared vocabulary fixes and which communication form was used for the decision at hand, and the review decides on artifacts developed without the affected units or settled in writing where the decision was open-ended, producing a rework or a re-run in a richer form.
information_or2: Artifact with the stakeholders who participated and their unit, the communication form used and the equivocality of the decision it served, and the vocabulary entry with its agreed definition, bound to artifact, decision, role and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The facilitating architect creates and answers for the participation record; each participating unit confirms its involvement; the vocabulary owner answers for the agreed definitions.

label: Transparency over the actual landscape and its dependencies
text_anchor: "transparency over complexity, dependencies, and actual (not idealized) structure". N6 requires dependency data to be collected rather than assumed, and N7 continuous lineage between planning and operational data.
use_or1: The architect scoping a transformation reads which applications a change touches and which dependencies it crosses, and decides on the scope and sequence, producing a recorded scoping decision with the dependencies accepted as in scope.
information_or2: Application-to-application dependency with its direction and the data objects that flow across it, the source from which the dependency was established and the date it was last confirmed, bound to application, interface and data object.
producer_or3: The Application Architect confirms the dependencies and data flows of the applications in their scope, and automated discovery over integration configurations and diagrams proposes dependencies that no architect had recorded, each remaining a candidate until the Application Architect accepts or edits it.

label: EA delivered as a continuous service
text_anchor: "EA delivered as a continuous service (not a document product) whose diagnostic, actionable, strategic-insight artifacts drive decision quality".
use_or1: A decision-maker requests an architecture service for a pending decision, and the architecture function decides on acceptance, scope and delivery date, producing a recorded engagement tied to the decision it serves.
information_or2: Architecture service request with the requesting role, the decision it serves, the artifact delivered and the date, bound to role, decision and artifact.
producer_or3: The requesting role creates the request; the architecture function answers for acceptance and delivery; the decision record confirms which artifact informed it.

label: Strategy-driven, future-oriented EA process
text_anchor: "a top-down, business-strategy-driven, future-oriented EA process as the leading quality indicator". N5 fixes scope through as-is, to-be and a transition plan.
use_or1: The lead architect records for each architecture effort the business goal that drives it and the as-is, to-be and transition artifacts it must produce, and the review decides on efforts that have no driving goal or no target state, producing a redirection or closure decision.
information_or2: Architecture effort with the business goal driving it, its as-is, to-be and transition artifacts and their status, bound to goal, artifact and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The lead architect creates and answers for the effort record; the business owner of the driving goal confirms it; each artifact owner confirms delivery.

label: EA function sized, structured and placed for its required reach
text_anchor: "EA function sizing, specialization, structure, and corporate placement matched to organization size, diversification, and required authority". N6 requires roles defined with specific responsibilities rather than generic labels.
use_or1: The head of architecture records the architecture roles with their specialisation and placement together with the organisational facts the arrangement is meant to match — unit size, degree of diversification and the authority the function needs — and decides at the annual review which parts of the landscape no architect covers and where the arrangement no longer matches those facts, producing a staffing, placement or reassignment decision.
information_or2: Architecture role with its specialisation, reporting placement and the units and landscape areas it covers, together with the recorded size, diversification and required authority the placement was matched against and the date that match was last reviewed, bound to role, person and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The head of architecture creates and answers for the role and coverage record; each architect confirms the area they cover; the receiving unit confirms the embedded placement.

label: Stage-appropriate capability development
text_anchor: "developed in stage-appropriate steps, with planning ambitions and expected contributions matched to the capability currently available". N5 decomposes capability building into discrete blocks.
use_or1: The head of architecture records which architecture practices are established, which block is planned next and what contribution the function is expected to make at the stage now reached, and decides on requests that assume a practice not yet in place, producing a deferral or a capability-building decision.
information_or2: Architecture practice with its established or planned status, the capability block it belongs to, the planned next step with its date, and the contribution expected from the function at the current stage, bound to the architecture function and the practice.
producer_or3: The head of architecture creates and answers for the practice inventory and the plan; the architect operating each practice confirms that it is established.

label: EA sensing, mobilizing and transforming activity
text_anchor: "EA sensing/mobilizing/transforming as a dynamic capability" and "continuous EA-grounded sense-making".
use_or1: The architect records each sensing observation, the mobilisation decision it triggered and the transforming action that followed, and the review decides per stage on items that have not moved — an observation without a mobilisation decision, a mobilisation without a transforming action — producing a pursue, reassign or close decision.
information_or2: Sensing observation with its source and date, the mobilisation decision with the resources it released, the transforming action with the model or process change it produced, and the sense-making step that connects them, bound to observation, decision, initiative and architecture artifact.
producer_or3: The observing architect creates the observation, the deciding body records the mobilisation and the resources released, and the initiative owner reports the transforming action and the artifact it changed.

label: Indirect, configuration-dependent EA value realization
text_anchor: "EA value realized indirectly through mediators (alignment, process innovation, decision-making), gated by conversion factors and equifinal EAM configurations, moderated by organizational context".
use_or1: Met. The architecture leadership would decide on which conversion factors to strengthen if the value chain and its gating factors were established, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. The claim is that architecture value arises through a chain of mediators gated by conversion factors and moderated by context. Establishing that chain requires a causal model relating architecture work to benefit, which the framework explicitly does not supply and which no enterprise object carries. Recording architecture activity and recording benefits separately would leave the mediation itself unrepresented, and asserting the link from their co-occurrence would be an unjustified proxy. CF#29 and CF#362 confirm that more than one configuration is sufficient and that no single implementation model holds.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Agile, iterative architecture practice
text_anchor: "agile, business-focused, iterative EA (backlogs, interim states, integrator roles)". N5 records that sequential planning is retained for critical processes and enterprise-wide releases.
use_or1: The lead architect maintains an architecture backlog and the interim target states between the current and the end state, and decides per planning cycle which interim state the next increment must reach, producing a committed increment with an owner.
information_or2: Architecture backlog item with priority and status, the interim target state it serves, the end state, the integrator role assigned and the planning mode applied, bound to initiative, artifact and role.
producer_or3: The lead architect creates and answers for the backlog and the interim states; the integrator confirms the assignment; the delivery team reports increment status in the existing cycle.

label: Composable, loosely coupled platform architecture
text_anchor: "Composable/modular, loosely coupled, federated platform architectures (packaged business capabilities, data mesh, vendor-agnostic mappings)".
use_or1: The architect reviewing a change decides whether it stays within the module boundary and its published interface, producing an approval or a condition to route the change through the interface rather than around it.
information_or2: Capability module with its boundary, the interface it publishes and the version of that interface, the couplings that cross the boundary and whether each uses the published interface, bound to application, capability and interface.
producer_or3: The module owner creates and answers for the boundary and the published interface; the consuming application owner confirms which interface version they use.

label: Capability-based identification and scoping of initiatives
text_anchor: "Business capability maps, value streams, and capability-based planning as the method for identifying, prioritizing, and scoping transformation initiatives".
use_or1: The planner scopes an initiative against the capabilities it changes and the value stream it serves, and the portfolio review decides on initiatives that name no capability, producing a rescoping or rejection decision.
information_or2: Capability with its position in the map, strategic importance and supporting applications; the ordered Value Stream Stages it enables and their Value Stream; and the initiative that changes it, bound to capability, stage, Value Stream, application and initiative.
producer_or3: The Capability Owner confirms the capability, its strategic importance and the applications mapped to it. The Business Stakeholder creates and confirms the Value Stream and its ordered Stages, and confirms their capability mappings together with the Capability Owner. The Initiative Owner confirms which capabilities their initiative changes. Model-proposed initiative-to-capability mappings remain candidates until the Initiative Owner accepts or edits them.

label: Architecture governance and coherence
text_anchor: "project conformance", "formal/informal control portfolios", "automated verification" and "reconciliation with portfolio management". N2 specifies operational evidence, N4 joint roadmapping.
use_or1: The reviewing architect decides per undertaking on conformance, exception or condition, and the decision produces a recorded architecture decision with a measure and a due date, while the portfolio leadership decides on scheduling conflicts between dependent applications in the joint plan. Part of the checking runs by machine: the application derives conformance findings from the machine-readable integration profiles under a disclosed rule, and the architect decides per finding on confirmation, exception or condition.
information_or2: Rule with version, object checked and check result, control type applied, architecture decision with exception and measure, and dependency and plan state, bound to undertaking, application and rule. The machine check adds the integration profile per application, the disclosed check rule and the conformance finding derived from it.
producer_or3: The architecture board creates and answers for the rules including their version, the architect of the undertaking under review creates the conformance evidence, and the portfolio leadership creates the plan states. The integration profiles are maintained by the application owners, and the application derives the conformance findings from them deterministically under a disclosed rule.

label: Architecture spanning legally distinct organizations
text_anchor: "Extended enterprise architecture spanning legally distinct organizations and ecosystems, with explicit viability factors and its typical lead-organization asymmetry".
use_or1: The architect records for each interface that leaves the enterprise which counterpart it reaches and which viability condition it depends on, and decides on interfaces whose condition is unmet, producing a mitigation or discontinuation decision.
information_or2: Cross-boundary interface with the counterpart it reaches as an attribute of the interface, the data it carries, the viability condition it depends on and the lead role in the arrangement, bound to application and interface.
producer_or3: The owner of the internal application at the boundary creates and answers for the interface record and its viability condition, and the architecture board confirms the lead role assumed.

label: EA modeling foundations for traceability
text_anchor: "typed, traceable links from strategy to operations" and "partially automatable". N5 requires synchronisation, N7 the checking of expected model inconsistencies.
use_or1: The architect responsible for the model decides per consistency finding on correction, completion or rejection, and on ambiguity decides personally rather than letting the synchronisation run automatically, which produces a task with an owner per finding.
information_or2: Model element with version, typed relationship between model elements across layers, mapping to application or process, the disclosed check logic and the consistency finding derived from it.
producer_or3: The architect named for the respective model creates and maintains elements and relationships, the application owner confirms the mapping of their application, and the application derives the consistency findings deterministically under a disclosed rule.

label: AI-augmented EA practice under explicit governance
text_anchor: "role shift to curator/validator", "maturity-staged AI governance" and "known reliability limits".
use_or1: The architect reviews each model-proposed entry as curator and validator and decides to accept, edit or reject it, and the architecture board decides which tasks may be delegated to a model at the governance stage currently in force, producing both a confirmed entry with its grounds and a recorded delegation rule.
information_or2: Model-proposed entry with the model and prompt version, the stated confidence, the validating architect, the decision and its grounds; the governance stage in force with the delegation rules and controls it carries; and the readiness precondition per domain with its status, bound to the proposed object, the validating role and the architecture function. The readiness domains are the four CF#510 names — infrastructure and skilled personnel, data governance maturity, legal and system compatibility, and strategic alignment — rather than a single generic readiness statement.
producer_or3: The model produces the proposal and the architecture function answers for the validation decision. The architecture board creates and answers for the delegation rules of the current governance stage, and the owner of each readiness precondition confirms its status.

label: Recorded adoption preconditions and staged obstacle resolution
text_anchor: "regulatory pressure, sponsorship, co-investment, institutional articulation, staged obstacle resolution, and adoption-readiness elements".
use_or1: The architecture lead records the named sponsor, the co-investment committed and the obstacles identified for an adoption step, and decides at each stage gate whether the preconditions are met, producing a proceed or hold decision with the outstanding obstacle named.
information_or2: Adoption step with its named sponsor, the co-investment committed, the regulatory or institutional driver invoked, the obstacles identified and their resolution status, bound to organisational unit, role and adoption step.
producer_or3: The architecture lead creates and answers for the adoption record; the named sponsor confirms the sponsorship and the committed co-investment; the obstacle owner reports resolution.

label: Governed data foundation with stewarded quality
text_anchor: "Data quality management and data governance (including security and common data infrastructure) as a foundational enabling condition".
use_or1: The data steward reviews the fields under their stewardship against the trusted source, the agreed update cadence and the protection the field’s classification requires, and decides on fields that are stale, lack a trusted source or are held outside the common data infrastructure, producing a correction, a reclassification or a migration decision.
information_or2: Data field with its steward, trusted source, sensitivity classification and the access rule that follows from it, the agreed update cadence, the date last synchronised, and the platform of the common data infrastructure that holds it, bound to data field, standard, application and platform.
producer_or3: The named steward creates and answers for the field definition, the trusted source and the classification; the source system owner confirms the synchronisation date; the platform owner confirms where the field is held.

label: Robust, flexible, integrable technology infrastructure
text_anchor: "Robust, flexible, integrable technology infrastructure". N2 specifies technical expertise and continuing investment.
use_or1: The architect of an undertaking checks its technical requirements against the evidenced properties of the systems and interfaces concerned, and that produces a feasibility decision: approval, a condition for a preceding measure, or rejection of the technical scope.
information_or2: Technical requirement of the undertaking, operating and recovery evidence, result of a change or integration test with scope and source, bound to application, interface and environment.
producer_or3: The operations function of the respective platform creates the operating and recovery evidence, and the implementing team creates the change and integration test evidence. Both producers carry the evidenced property per system, not a summary claim about the estate.

label: Analytics capability
text_anchor: "analytics capability".
use_or1: The analytics owner checks the analysis demand of a planned undertaking against available data sources, their verified reliability and the analysis competence on hand, and that produces a decision on feasibility or a sourcing or qualification measure.
information_or2: Required analysis, data source drawn on, result of its reliability check and the named analysis competence, bound to undertaking, application and team.
producer_or3: The data owner of the respective source creates provenance and quality statements; the line manager confirms the competence statement for their team.

label: Accompanying organizational and governance measures per technology initiative
text_anchor: "People, organizational, and governance dimensions established alongside (or before) technology investment".
use_or1: The programme lead reviews per technology initiative which accompanying organisational and governance measures are defined and what status they hold, and decides at the release gate on initiatives whose accompanying measures lag, producing a hold or a resequencing decision.
information_or2: Technology initiative with its accompanying people, organisational and governance measures, each with owner, planned date and status, bound to initiative and role.
producer_or3: The initiative owner creates and answers for the accompanying measures; the owner of each measure confirms its status.

label: Systematic sensing activity
text_anchor: "Systematic sensing: scouting, scenario planning, cross-industry brokering, inside-out infrastructure sensing, and deliberate absorptive filtering".
use_or1: The responsible scout records an observation with its source and the scenario it bears on, and the review decides which observations are admitted for further work and which are filtered out, producing a recorded admission decision with its reason.
information_or2: Observation with source, date and the scenario or capability it bears on, the filtering decision and its reason, bound to observation, scenario and capability.
producer_or3: The scouting role creates and answers for the observation; the reviewing body records the admission or filtering decision in its minutes.

label: Rapid seizing of sensed opportunities
text_anchor: "Rapid seizing of sensed opportunities: strategic agility, speed, scale elasticity, solution-centric restructuring".
use_or1: The deciding body records the decision taken on an admitted opportunity, the resources committed and whether the commitment can be scaled up or released again, and decides at review on opportunities past their decision deadline and on commitments that cannot be released, producing a decision, a restructuring of the delivery arrangement, or a documented closure.
information_or2: Admitted opportunity with its admission date and decision deadline, the decision taken, the resources committed and their elasticity — whether they can be scaled or released and on what notice — and the delivery arrangement formed around the solution, bound to observation, decision, initiative and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The body deciding on the opportunity creates and answers for the decision and the committed resources; the unit supplying the resources confirms the elasticity it can offer; the initiative owner records the delivery arrangement formed.

label: Institutionalizing transformation actions
text_anchor: "Ecosystem navigation, structural redesign, and maturity-building capability to institutionalize transformation".
use_or1: The transformation lead records for each transforming action the structural change it makes, the cross-boundary arrangements it depends on and the step that institutionalises it, and decides on actions that end without an institutionalisation step or that leave a cross-boundary dependency unresolved, producing an institutionalisation task or a documented exception.
information_or2: Transforming action with its type and completion date, the structural change it makes to units or roles, the cross-boundary interfaces and dependencies it relies on, and the standard, role or process it was institutionalised into, bound to initiative, organisational unit, interface and standard.
producer_or3: The transformation lead creates and answers for the action record and the structural change; the owner of the internal application at each boundary confirms the cross-boundary dependency, as for the interfaces held under CC32-A1; the owner of the receiving standard, role or process confirms the handover.

label: Sequenced and paced change orchestration
text_anchor: "structured change management, stage-appropriate sequencing, pacing, and contingent configuration of levers".
use_or1: The programme lead maintains the sequence of change steps with their dependencies and planned pace, and decides at each stage gate whether the next step may start, producing a release or a hold with the blocking dependency named.
information_or2: Change step with its stage, planned start and end, the dependencies it waits on and the levers configured for it, bound to initiative, programme and dependency.
producer_or3: The programme lead creates and answers for the sequence and the stage decisions; the owner of each dependency confirms its readiness.

label: Adaptive organizational structures
text_anchor: "separation-vs-integration decisions", "experimentation tracks" and "recursive centralization-decentralization recalibration". N5 explicitly names "people moving between an innovation unit and the core".
use_or1: The transformation initiative leadership decides per undertaking on separation from or integration into the core and sets a review date, and at that date a confirmation or correction of the scoping decision follows, while every experiment ends with a follow-up decision on continuation, handover or discontinuation.
information_or2: Scoping decision with rationale, organisational units involved, period and review date, hypothesis, result and follow-up decision of the experiment, and the temporary assignment of a person between units.
producer_or3: The deciding leadership creates and answers for the scoping decision, the experiment owner creates the result report, and the releasing and receiving team leads jointly create the transfer agreement.

label: Pre-built surge, continuity and learning arrangements
text_anchor: "IT service quality, governance maturity, adaptive governance behavior, surge capacity, and learning" as the arrangements built in advance.
use_or1: The service owner records the standby capacity and continuity provision for a critical application and the learning captured after each incident, and the review decides on applications whose provision falls short of their criticality, producing a remediation task with an owner.
information_or2: Critical application with its continuity provision, recovery expectation, standby arrangement and the learning recorded after incidents, bound to application, environment and role.
producer_or3: The service owner creates and answers for the continuity and standby record; the incident owner records the learning after each incident.

label: Organizational resilience and antifragility
text_anchor: "Resilience/antifragility built through ..." as a property of the organisation, with "disruption alone does not create it".
use_or1: Met. The executive leadership would decide on where to strengthen resilience if the property were established, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed, and not for both halves in the same way. For resilience the evidence does supply measurement: CF#583 reports IT service quality and governance maturity as measured, non-redundant components of IT organisational resilience, and CF#257 describes an assessment combining three lenses. For antifragility it does not. CF#115 distinguishes the two explicitly and relates antifragility to slack resources without supplying an instrument for it. Because the aspect claims resilience and antifragility together, and a yes carries the whole claim of its aspect, the missing half decides the verdict. Should the aspect later be carried by an instrument that covers both, or should the two be separated on a textual basis, the verdict is to be revisited under the revision rule.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Sustained executive sponsorship
text_anchor: "Sustained executive sponsorship" as the first of the two combined enablers.
use_or1: The programme lead records the named executive sponsor for each initiative together with the sponsor decisions and resource commitments made, and the review decides on initiatives whose sponsor has taken no decision in the review period, producing a re-sponsorship or closure decision.
information_or2: Initiative with its named executive sponsor, the sponsor decisions taken with their dates and the resources committed, bound to initiative, programme and person.
producer_or3: The sponsoring executive answers for their own decisions and commitments, recorded through the existing decision process; the programme lead confirms the sponsor assignment.

label: Cross-functional collaboration in transformation work
text_anchor: "cross-functional collaboration as the pervasive capability-building enabler".
use_or1: The initiative lead records the work items that two or more functions carry jointly and the decisions taken together, and the review decides on initiatives that affect a function which contributes no joint item and no joint decision, producing a participation, rescoping or escalation decision.
information_or2: Joint work item or decision with the functions that carried it and the role each held, the artifact it produced, and the units the initiative affects, bound to initiative, work item, decision and organisational unit.
producer_or3: Each contributing function confirms its own contribution to the joint item, and the initiative lead answers for the record of joint decisions taken. Representation alone is not recorded as collaboration.

label: Digital leadership roles with a granted mandate
text_anchor: "CDO/transformation units, cross-functional governance bodies, and digital leadership ... granted genuine enterprise-level authority".
use_or1: The governance owner records which decision domains a digital leadership role or transformation unit holds rights in, and decides on matters escalated to a role that holds no right in the domain concerned, producing a reassignment or an extension of its rights.
information_or2: Digital leadership role or unit with the decision domains it holds rights in, the reach of each right across organisational units, the granting body and the validity period, bound to role, body, decision domain and organisational unit. A mandate title without named decision domains is recorded as incomplete.
producer_or3: The body granting the rights creates and answers for them, and the role holder confirms acceptance. The record carries the decision rights actually assigned, which is what makes the granted authority checkable rather than asserted. Whether the executive tier stands behind those rights in practice is the condition under which the arrangement works, which CF#144 and CF#145 state as such, and falls under the general boundary of every positive verdict.

label: Skill development, role redefinition and talent acquisition
text_anchor: "Digital skill development, role redefinition, talent acquisition". The clause that skills consistently lag strategy maturity states the consequence.
use_or1: The line manager records the redefined role with the skills it requires and the development or hiring measure that closes the gap, and the review decides on roles whose required skills have no measure, producing a development, hiring or rescoping decision.
information_or2: Role with its required skills, the skills held in the team, the gap identified and the development or hiring measure addressing it with owner and date, bound to role, person and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The line manager creates and answers for the role definition and the gap; the personnel function confirms the hiring measure; the individual confirms the development measure.

label: Management digital competence at an agreed level
text_anchor: "management digital competence" as a distinct element of the condition.
use_or1: The line manager and the person agree a competence level per skill category on the enterprise scale and record it, and the personnel function decides which cohorts fall below the level a role requires, producing a mandatory training assignment with a due date. An assignment not completed by that date returns to the manager for decision.
information_or2: Skill category with the agreed competence level on the enterprise scale from 1 to 5, the date and parties of the agreement, the level the role requires, and the mandatory training assigned with its completion status, bound to person, role, skill category and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The line manager and the person jointly produce the agreed level in the existing assessment conversation and answer for it, and the training system supplies the completion record for the assigned mandatory training. The enterprise supplies the operational definition here — the scale with its five ordered levels and the agreed assessment as the rule of interpretation — rather than the RQ1 evidence. What the record carries is the agreed level and the completed training, not an independent measurement of competence.

label: Employee participation in transformation initiatives
text_anchor: "Employee participation". N4 supports early involvement, N6 the careful interpretation of negative experiences.
use_or1: The initiative leadership decides on every contribution received and records the decision with its rationale, which produces an answered response to the contributing person and, where the contribution is accepted, an agreed measure with an owner and a due date.
information_or2: Initiative and phase, contribution submitted, reported experience with the need affected, response decision and agreed measure, bound to initiative, contributing person and responsible role.
producer_or3: The contributing employee creates the contribution and the experience record themselves and remains their source; the initiative leadership creates the response decision and the measure agreement. Both carry exactly what the record claims: a reported perspective and a decision taken.

label: Sentiment and active willingness to participate
text_anchor: "grounded in sentiment" and "converts employees' predispositions into active willingness to take part in transformation". N1: "sentiment cannot be instructed into existence".
use_or1: Met. The initiative leadership would take an intervention decision on the basis of an established sentiment, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. What is missing is a reasoned operational definition for sentiment and actual willingness to participate — a reference group, ordered levels and a rule of interpretation. The evidence describes the relationship between earlier experiences, sentiment and willingness without supplying an instrument that measures it, which is the difference from CC50, where the evidence names the dimensions with their scales. Without such a definition, contributions and experience records would stand in for the inner state as an unjustified proxy. The form of elicitation is not what decides this: a self-report administered under a validated instrument would carry the measured disposition, and one administered without a rule of interpretation carries only the statement made.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Individual managerial readiness dispositions
text_anchor: "Individual managerial readiness (strategy, structure, technology dispositions) as a distinct micro-foundational precondition not reducible to organizational readiness".
use_or1: The personnel function administers the managerial readiness instrument to the named manager population and decides per dimension which cohort receives targeted preparation, producing a measure with an owner and a date.
information_or2: Instrument with its version and the three dimensions it measures — digital structure readiness per CF#277, digital technology readiness per CF#278 and digital strategy readiness per CF#279, the strongest of the three — the items, the responses, the survey date and the dimension-level result under the instrument’s own rules, bound to survey run, manager cohort and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The producers of the information are the responding managers, who answer the instrument’s items, together with the personnel function that administers the survey and answers for its conduct. The instrument is the operational definition rather than a producer: CF#277, CF#278 and CF#279 name its three dimensions with their scales and reported coefficients. What the record carries is the disposition as that instrument defines and measures it, not a general statement about managerial quality.

label: Bi-directional communication and engagement practice
text_anchor: "built via bi-directional communication and positive engagement".
use_or1: The initiative lead records each engagement exchange with the stakeholder group, the question raised and the response given, and the review decides on questions left unanswered past their due date, producing a response task with an owner.
information_or2: Engagement exchange with its stakeholder group, date, the question raised, the response given and its date, bound to initiative, organisational unit and role.
producer_or3: The raising stakeholder creates the question and remains its source; the initiative lead answers for the response record.

label: Stakeholder trust and psychological ownership
text_anchor: "Trust and psychological ownership as the mechanism securing buy-in and governance effectiveness".
use_or1: Met. The initiative leadership would decide on corrective engagement if the level of trust and ownership were established, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. Trust and psychological ownership are states held by the stakeholders. Exchange records evidence the practice, not the state, and no reasoned operational definition with a reference group and a rule of interpretation is available. Inferring trust from exchange volume would be an unjustified proxy.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Cultural substrate of transformation
text_anchor: "Risk tolerance, experimentation, innovation mindset, collaboration, learning, and information openness as cultural substrate". N1 names "shared dispositions", N2 states that they are "not established by instruction".
use_or1: Met. The undertaking leadership would take a decision on measures on the basis of an established cultural substrate, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. The claim asserts risk tolerance, innovation mindset, collaboration, learning and information openness as a *shared substrate*. Individual experiment, knowledge or exchange records do not evidence that shared property, and without a reasoned operational definition covering reference group and rule of interpretation an unjustified proxy would stand in its place. CF#195 records explicitly that the culture attributes of maturity models yield no ready validated instrument. The documentable individual practices do not carry the claim of this aspect, and a yes for a part is not sufficient.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Core values filtering transformation decisions
text_anchor: "core values filter transformation decisions".
use_or1: The deciding role records the declared value reference when taking a transformation decision, and a contradiction between a declared value and the decision taken is raised for clarification in the review, which produces a confirmed or corrected decision.
information_or2: Declared core value, the transformation decision taken and the rationale for its value reference, bound to decision, undertaking and value catalogue.
producer_or3: The executive leadership creates and answers for the declared value catalogue; the deciding role creates the rationale for the value reference in the existing decision process. Both carry the declared value, which CF#297 explicitly leaves open as a limit.

label: Capacity in resources and structure
text_anchor: "with capacity (resources/structure) as a distinct antecedent".
use_or1: The programme lead records the capacity a change step requires against the capacity the affected units have committed, and decides on steps that start without committed capacity, producing a hold or a rescheduling decision.
information_or2: Change step with the capacity it requires, the capacity committed by each affected unit and the structural provision made, bound to initiative, organisational unit and role.
producer_or3: The affected unit leadership creates and answers for the committed capacity; the programme lead answers for the requirement.

label: Shared change valence and change efficacy
text_anchor: "Shared change valence and change efficacy as a collective property".
use_or1: Met. The programme leadership would decide on corrective measures if the collective readiness were established, and a measure with an owner would follow.
information_or2: Failed. The claim asserts valence and efficacy as shared across a group. Capacity records and participation records do not carry a collective belief, and no reasoned operational definition with a reference group and a rule of interpretation is available. Aggregating individual statements without such a definition would be an unjustified proxy.
producer_or3: Not testable, because without specified information there is no object for a producer.

label: Structured change communication and sponsor cascade
text_anchor: "Change narratives, cascading sponsorship, frame-of-reference communication, and momentum-building decomposition".
use_or1: The change lead records the narrative, the sponsor cascade and the communication issued per stage, and the review decides on units the cascade has not reached, producing a targeted communication task with an owner and a date.
information_or2: Change stage with its narrative, the sponsors in the cascade and the units each reaches, the communication issued and its date, bound to initiative, organisational unit and role.
producer_or3: The change lead creates and answers for the narrative and the communication record; each sponsor in the cascade confirms the communication they issued.

label: Multi-dimensional assessment architecture
text_anchor: "validated multi-dimensional structures" and "dimension-level (not only aggregate) evaluation". The enabling statement additionally requires the strategic need to be judged separately.
use_or1: The assessment team decides on the basis of the dimension-level results which gaps are addressed first and assigns an owner per gap, which produces a prioritised list of measures with due dates.
information_or2: Chosen instrument with its version, the validation evidence published for it and the suitability rationale for this context of use, its dimensions and items, the responses collected, the survey date, the due date for re-assessment and the dimension-level result under the instrument’s evaluation rules, bound to organisational unit and survey.
producer_or3: The producers of the information are the respondents the chosen instrument provides for, who answer its items, together with the assessment team that administers the survey and answers for its conduct. The instrument is the operational definition rather than a producer, and it comes with the validation evidence published for it; MIG per CF#556 and DORAM per CF#134 and CF#135 are the two present in the evidence. The evaluation follows the instrument’s disclosed rule. CF#251 bounds the claim: there is no consensual cross-sector instrument and the empirical validation is often limited, so the record holds the validation evidence that exists for the chosen instrument rather than asserting that it is validated.

label: Multi-perspective assessment design
text_anchor: "multi-assessor panels, employee-vs-leadership triangulation, validated instruments, and interview-corrected self-assessment".
use_or1: The assessment lead records the panel composition, the perspectives covered and the correction step applied, and decides on assessments run from a single perspective, producing a re-run or a qualified reporting decision.
information_or2: Assessment run with its panel members and the perspective each represents, the instrument used together with its published validation evidence, the correction step applied and the deviation found between perspectives, bound to assessment run, role and organisational unit.
producer_or3: The assessment lead creates and answers for the panel and the correction step; each panel member confirms their own participation; the validation evidence comes from the publication of the instrument used. Where an instrument carries no published validation, the record holds that absence rather than a validity claim.

label: Assessment converted into owned action
text_anchor: "Converting assessment into action: KPIs, thresholds, recommendation engines, roadmaps, continuous reassessment procedures".
use_or1: A detected gap is assigned to a named action owner with a due date and a recommended action derived from the rule that raised it, the owner works it from a self-service view of their own gaps, and the review decides on gaps whose action has passed its date, producing an escalation or a documented acceptance. Gaps with a common cause are sequenced into a roadmap rather than worked singly.
information_or2: Detected gap with the rule or threshold that raised it, the recommended action attached to that rule, the action owner, the due date, the action status, the roadmap step it belongs to and the reassessment date, bound to the object assessed, the owning role and the roadmap.
producer_or3: The rule defined by the responsible function raises the gap deterministically, and the named action owner answers for the action and its status.

label: Declared construct distinction in assessment design
text_anchor: "Readiness (behaviors, willingness, cyclical system) formally distinguished from maturity (implementation status) as an assessment precondition".
use_or1: The assessment lead records for each instrument and each dimension which construct it measures, and decides on instruments mixing both without saying so, producing a rejection or a separation of the dimensions before the assessment runs.
information_or2: Instrument dimension with the construct it measures, the rationale for that classification and the validity of the decision, bound to instrument, dimension and assessment run.
producer_or3: The assessment lead takes and answers for the classification, which is a documented design decision about the instrument in use rather than a statement about the organisation.

label: Resource and capability constraints with substitution mechanisms
text_anchor: "SME resource, skill, and R&D constraints with substitution mechanisms (intermediaries, collaboration)". N5 names partners and intermediaries, N6 the resources actually available.
use_or1: The undertaking leadership decides during planning whether the required competence is available internally or is supplemented through a partner contribution, and that produces an adjusted scoping decision or a confirmed partner agreement with service and availability.
information_or2: Available resource and competence per organisational unit, the constraint identified, the agreed partner contribution with service and availability, and the reasoned adjustment decision, bound to organisational unit, undertaking and partner.
producer_or3: The leadership of the organisational unit concerned creates and answers for the resource and competence statement for its area; the contracting owner creates the partner agreement. CF#109 limits the claim: the record holds the concrete constraint and does not infer it from company size.

label: SME-adapted model choice
text_anchor: "SME-adapted models instead of scaled-down large-firm approaches" and "Framework application is calibrated to small- and medium-sized-enterprise resource and capability constraints" in the enabling statement.
use_or1: The undertaking leadership chooses the model for viewing capabilities and competences for the organisational unit concerned and justifies the choice against its identified resource and capability constraints, which produces a documented model choice due for confirmation at the next planning round. A model choice without a rationale link produces a clarification task.
information_or2: Chosen model, its rationale, the reference to the identified constraints and the validity of the choice, bound to organisational unit and undertaking. The calibration claim is carried because the rationale binds to the constraint statements held under CC61-A1. Under the delimitation rule a documented choice of method is a documented practice and therefore bindable to an enterprise object.
producer_or3: The undertaking leadership takes and answers for the model choice; the leadership of the organisational unit concerned supplies, through CC61-A1, the constraint statement the rationale rests on.

label: Disciplined sourcing with recorded co-design and mediation
text_anchor: "Disciplined ecosystem partnering, vendor co-design, external mediation, and explicit build-vs-outsource competence decisions".
use_or1: The initiative lead records for each required competence the build-or-source decision with its reason, and where it is sourced, the co-design arrangement and any mediation engaged, and the review decides on competences sourced without a recorded reason or on co-design arrangements without a named internal counterpart, producing a confirmation or a resourcing change.
information_or2: Required competence with the build-or-source decision and its reason, the co-design arrangement with the internal role that carries it and the artifacts produced jointly, the mediation engaged with its purpose, and the validity of the decision, bound to initiative, capability and role. The external counterpart is held as an attribute of the decision.
producer_or3: The initiative lead takes and answers for the build-or-source decision and the mediation engaged; the capability owner confirms the competence requirement; the internal role named in the co-design arrangement confirms the joint artifacts produced.

label: Recorded context factors and the adaptations resting on them
text_anchor: "Transformation approaches conditioned by sector, region, regulation, and institutional context".
use_or1: The programme lead records the sector, regional and regulatory factors that apply to a unit and the adaptations the approach makes for them, and the review decides on adaptations whose factor no longer applies, producing a confirmation or a reversal.
information_or2: Context factor with its recorded value and validity, the adaptation that rests on it and the unit it applies to, bound to organisational unit, initiative and factor.
producer_or3: The unit leadership creates and answers for the factor values for its own area, and the compliance function confirms the regulatory factors in force.

label: Documented framework adaptation decisions
text_anchor: "Treating EA frameworks as adaptable means rather than prescriptive ends" and "pragmatic trade-offs, lightweight principles".
use_or1: The architecture board records which framework elements are adopted, which are adapted and which are set aside, with the reason for each, and decides on a request to reintroduce a set-aside element, producing a confirmation or a revision of the adaptation.
information_or2: Framework element with its adoption status, the adaptation made, the reason recorded and the validity of the decision, bound to the architecture function and the practice affected.
producer_or3: The architecture board takes and answers for the adaptation decision, and the architect operating the affected practice confirms that the adapted element is the one in use.

label: Committed investment balanced across technology and human capital
text_anchor: "Sufficient committed investment" and "balanced technology-and-human-capital allocation". N3 states that technology investment without matching skills lacks the capacity to be used.
use_or1: The programme lead reviews per initiative whether the committed budget covers both the technology and the associated skill build, and decides on release or on a resourcing condition that must be met first.
information_or2: Committed amount and period, its split between technology and human-capital lines, and the skill build associated with the technology investment, bound to initiative and programme.
producer_or3: The budget owner for the programme creates and answers for the commitment record, and the line manager of the affected team confirms the skill-build allocation.

label: Funding model matched to transformation dynamics
text_anchor: "funding models matched to transformation dynamics (portfolio/usage-based rather than stage-gate only)". N4 states that fixed upfront allocation assumes a predictable consumption that elastic digital services do not show.
use_or1: The portfolio lead records which funding model applies to an initiative and decides at the review whether that model still fits the consumption the initiative actually shows, which produces a confirmation or a change of funding model.
information_or2: Funding model in force, the review date, and the consumption pattern observed against it, bound to initiative and programme.
producer_or3: The finance partner for the programme creates and answers for the funding-model record, and the initiative owner reports the observed consumption in the existing reporting cycle.
